target_customer: High volume plaintiff law firms that run paid lead intake teams
problem: Law firms lose signed cases because leads are answered slowly or inconsistently by human intake staff, which wastes ad spend.
business_model: B2B software and service for law firm intake with a setup fee (a $3,000 fee is mentioned on the YC page) and ongoing subscription; pricing not public
product_category: Legal AI intake platform (voice and text agents, call coaching, CRM integrations)

founders.name: Ethan Hilton
education: Carnegie Mellon University, AI and Business, dropped out
previous_startups: Legal leads startup started at 16 that reached five figure MRR (per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Per YC page and a CMU Tepper news story.

founders.name: Ayushman
prior_employers: Chief Data Scientist at India's first unicorn (per YC page, company not named)
education: Carnegie Mellon University, MS in AI
founders.background_notes: Surname not stated on the YC page. YC page says about five years of enterprise AI for Fortune 100 and led a fraud detection team for a 30M MAU delivery app.

founders.name: Tolen Schreid
previous_startups: Co-founded a game with 9,000 DAU at age 15 (per YC page)

technical_complexity.rationale: Voice and text agents integrated with several legal CRMs (Clio, Litify, Lead Docket, Salesforce) need reliable conversation handling and integration work, but rely on commodity voice models.

defensibility.rationale: Integration with legal CRMs and intake workflows creates some lock in, but general voice agent platforms offer legal templates and are easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Other legal intake AI products launched in 2025 (Eve in June 2025, Hona in March 2025). Nothing found about a copy or acquisition of Caseflood.

market_need_then: Plaintiff firms spend heavily on lead generation and depend on fast intake. A vendor cited a Clio 2024 study that only 40% of law firms answered phone calls. The founder had earlier run a legal leads business.

branding.domain_note: Uses caseflood.ai, a .ai domain, not the .com.

identity.mascot_or_character: Voice AI named Luna (per Legal Tech Monitor)
identity.visual_style: Clean minimal layout with product mockups
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and direct, short headlines such as Intake, solved

brand_strength.rationale: Trade press covered the funding but no source discusses the brand itself. The name describes the case flood the product aims to create.

outcome_analysis: Caseflood is active and announced a $3.2M round on 2025-07-30, about six months after its Winter 2025 batch, with named law firm customers and claimed gains in signed cases. Founder experience in legal lead generation fits the niche. Other AI intake vendors launching in 2025 make defensibility the key risk.
